text:
Alex: noticing sustained queue depth growth for model 'redwood-13b-infer' in ap-south-1 since ~01:00 UTC, peaking at 480 requests in-flight.
Mira: yikes, what's the current admission-control threshold?
Alex: it auto-degraded from 300 -> 200 to 120 due to node failures earlier, looks like we never bumped it back.
Tiago: node failures? which fault domain?
Alex: 3 GPU nodes in p3-subpool went into MaintDrain after nvlink flapping. ops-runner reported degraded NICs.
Priya: I'm on it, checking k8s events + GPU health logs.
sre-bot: alert: queue_depth(redwood-13b-infer, ap-south-1) > 400 for 12m. suggested action: reroute non-SLO traffic. :warning:
Tiago: Can we temporarily route lower-priority customers to redwood-7b-quant? quality tradeoff noted.
Mira: Yes, do it per-route. Add a policy that routes requests with plan!=enterprise to the 7b-quant variant. We need to protect latency SLOs for enterprise.
Alex: quick command I ran to check backlog:
```
kubectl -n inference get pods -l model=redwood-13b-infer -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,CPU:.spec.containers[*].resources.requests,GPU:.spec.containers[*].resources.limits,AGE:.metadata.creationTimestamp
```
Alex: also checked queue histogram: 50th=60ms, 95th=1.8s, 99th=4.2s.
Priya: rolling through node diagnostics now. NVLink errors show up at kernel ring level, vendor targeting a firmware patch but ETA ~48h.
Tiago: we can't wait 48h. Options: 1) preemptively cordon and failover pods onto other pools (costly), 2) surge a small dedicated burst pool in ap-south-1 (requires quota approval), 3) broaden routing to other regions (latency penalties), 4) lower admission control further and return 429s for non-critical flows.
Mira: let's do a mixed approach. Start per-route routing to 7b-quant for non-enterprise now, and open a temporary cross-region fallback to ap-southeast-2 for enterprise if latency <=120ms. Also prepare an eviction plan to free up 4 gpus from p3-subpool.
Alex: implemented the per-route policy, patched gateway config, and applied canary to 10% of traffic. Deployed rule id: route-ps-apac-2026-02.
Priya: cordoning two affected nodes to force pods to reschedule now: `kubectl drain node/gpu-p3-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
ops-runner: drain started, scheduler backfills onto p3-spare-1 pool but some pods hit memory pressure and OOMKilled. we need to reduce batch sizes on redwood-13b-infer during reschedule.
Tiago: reduce max_batch_size from 64 -> 32 for the model group in the runtime config, that halves peak memory. make sure to do this via config rollout, not restart.
Alex: config change applied to runtime config alias 'ap-south-1-runtime-v3' using: `redwoodctl deploy-config --alias ap-south-1-runtime-v3 --set model.redwood-13b-infer.max_batch=32`
Mira: good. Monitoring: queue_depth dropped from 480 -> 220 in 8m after routing + batch change. 95th latency still 2.1s but trending down.
Priya: vendor firmware ETA changed to 36h; still too long. We should request emergency quota for 4 GPUs in ap-south-1 to create a temporary burst pool. Ops is filing it now.
Tiago: cost note: bursting 4 A100s for 36h estimated extra $6.5k. Can finance sign off? If not, we continue routing and more aggressive admission control.
Mira: ok to escalate to finance but prefer the routing+batch approach and only burst if backlog re-surges past 400 again. Create a rollback/playbook for both scenarios.
Alex: creating a short playbook in the incident doc with steps: identify impacted model, enable per-route fallback, reduce batch, cordon nodes, request burst pool, and customer comms. Will paste link when ready.
Priya: adding a snippet to the playbook for triage checklist and exact queries: `sum(rate(queue_depth{model=\"redwood-13b-infer\",region=\"ap-south-1\"}[5m]))` and `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(response_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le))`
ops-runner: temporary note: added label `slo-protect=true` for enterprise routes so future automated reroutes will prefer those.
Mira: thanks team. Keep updates here every 15m. If queue_depth < 200 and 95th lat < 1.2s for 30m, we'll demote to postmortem. Otherwise, prep for burst. :thumbsup:
